Q: Python Reactivex and OpenAI -- Stream hangs? A:

to_iterable().run() blocks until the observable completes. In your case, completion isn’t guaranteed. With subscribe(print) you see values as they arrive, even if the stream never terminates. But run() waits for a terminal event.

If the async stream errors or exits early without calling on_completed() or on_error(), the observable stays open forever and run() hangs.

In patterns like this you need to ensure every execution path ends in either on_completed() or on_error(), and avoid calling blocking run() on the asyncio event loop. Otherwise a stalled or interrupted stream will look like an infinite hang.

For context only: issues like this are hard to diagnose after the fact because you can’t tell whether the stream stalled, errored, or never terminated cleanly.

Tools like AI Badgr focus on per-request receipts (timing, streaming stalls, failure stage) so this class of hang is explainable post-hoc.

Q: Python or Java script A:

You can build this system by separating ticket booking and luggage tracking as two linked modules, connected through a unique QR code per luggage item.

1. Ticket Booking (Normal Flow)

  • User searches route → selects bus → selects seat → books ticket

  • System generates:

    • ticketId

    • Passenger + seat details

  • Ticket QR (optional) for verification

2. Luggage Tracking System (Core Feature)

Key rule:
👉 Each luggage item gets its own QR code, linked to one ticket

Data Link

Ticket → Multiple Luggag

Each luggage record stores:

  • Ticket ID

  • Source

  • Destination

  • Current status

3. QR Code Logic

Each luggage QR contains:

{
  "ticketId": "TKT123",
  "luggageId": "LUG456"
}

QR is generated at booking time (or ticket issuing).

4. Luggage Status Flow (Scan-Based)

Boarding point LOADED
En route (optional) IN_TRANSIT

Destination OFFLOADED

5. User View

User can see luggage tracking:

Luggage Code: LUG-456
From: Delhi
To: Jaipur
Status: Offloaded

6. Admin Dashboard Features

Admin can:

  • Add buses (seat count & layout)

  • Add routes & schedules

  • Auto-generate seat maps based on seat count

  • Issue tickets (online/offline)

  • Scan luggage QR codes

  • View/export luggage list

7. Seat Map Logic

Seat map is generated dynamically from bus config:

totalSeats = 40
layout = 2x2

Booked seats are disabled using backend seat data.

8. Database Structure (Simplified)

Ticket

ticketId, busId, routeId, seatNumber

Luggage

luggageId,
ticketId,
status,
source,
destination,
logs[]

9. Tech Stack (Suggested)

  • Frontend: React

  • Backend: Node.js + Express

  • DB: MongoDB

  • QR: qrcode (generate), html5-qrcode (scan)

  • Auth: JWT (Admin / Staff / User roles)

10. Final Result

1- Normal bus booking system
2- Per-luggage QR tracking
3- Real-time status updates
4- Admin-controlled scanning
5- Clear luggage audit trail

Q: Azure SQL Managed Instance randomly freezes/locks up and must be Stopped/Restarted A:

Azure SQL Managed Instance itself is generally stable. When it appears to “freeze” and only recovers after a restart, the root cause is almost always resource saturation or blocking, not an Azure platform failure.

1. Check for blocking sessions

Long-running transactions or blocking chains can make the instance appear unresponsive:

SELECT *
FROM sys.dm_exec_requests
WHERE blocking_session_id <> 0;

If you see sustained LCK_M_* waits, identify the blocking query and optimize or terminate it.

2. Monitor CPU, memory, and IO usage

Review Azure Monitor metrics:

  • CPU percentage

  • Data IO percentage

  • Log IO percentage

Consistent usage above ~80–90% indicates the instance is undersized or workloads are not optimized.

3. Investigate tempdb pressure

High tempdb usage commonly causes severe slowdowns:

SELECT *
FROM sys.dm_db_file_space_usage;

Typical causes include large sorts, hash joins, cursors, and missing indexes.

4. Identify runaway queries or jobs

ETL processes, reports, or SQL Agent jobs can consume all resources unexpectedly:

SELECT session_id, status, wait_type, cpu_time, total_elapsed_time
FROM sys.dm_exec_sessions
WHERE is_user_process = 1;

Look for sessions with high CPU time or long elapsed duration.

5. Review maintenance activities

Index rebuilds and statistics updates during peak hours can block workloads.

Best practices:

  • Schedule maintenance during off-peak hours

  • Prefer REORGANIZE over REBUILD when possible

  • Use ONLINE = ON for rebuilds

    6. Enable Query Store

    Query Store helps identify query regressions that cause sudden performance degradation:

    ALTER DATABASE CURRENT SET QUERY_STORE = ON;

    Analyze top resource-consuming queries after freezes occur.

7. If restart temporarily resolves the issue

This typically indicates:

  • Memory pressure

  • Accumulated blocking

  • Unoptimized queries consuming resources over time

Scaling up the Managed Instance (vCores or memory) is often required.

8. Contact Microsoft support if needed

If freezes continue after optimization, open an Azure support ticket with:

  • Timestamp of the freeze

  • Azure Monitor metrics

  • Query Store data

They can investigate internal engine or infrastructure issues.

Conclusion

An Azure SQL Managed Instance that requires restarts is almost always affected by workload or resource issues. Proper monitoring, query optimization, maintenance scheduling, and capacity planning usually resolve the problem permanently.

Q: Anaconda: Failed to create process. Invoke-Expression : Cannot bind argument to parameter 'Command' because it is an empty string A:
